title: Absorptive buffer runway forecast — Oct 2024
summary: Working capacity-sheet to quantify the absorptive buffer (short-term extra capacity) required in each region to meet 95th-percentile spike demand and to size warm-failover reserves for multi-region DR. Focus is on runway (how many hours/days of spike we can absorb) and pragmatic mitigations for constrained regions.

assumptions: 95th percentile peak computed from last 90 days of QPS-per-GPU telemetry
Committed GPUs = on-demand reserved + Dedicated commitments; excludes spot salvage pools
Absorptive buffer defined as immediate-in-place capacity to accept spike without cold-provisioning new instances
Warm failover reserve = capacity kept warm in a different region, can take traffic within SLA drain window
Target reserve percent is fraction of total GPUs in-region to aim for redundancy
Network egress limits and cross-region bandwidth may increase SLA drain time by up to 30% for large failovers
forecast_summary: We recommend a 280-GPU global absorptive buffer (18% of fleet) with regional splits as shown. This provides ~30-36 hours of runway for median spike profiles at current token-per-request distribution, or 8-12 hours for extreme correlated spikes. For enterprise launch windows, temporarily increase warm-failover reserve in us-east4 and europe-west1 by +50% (40 GPUs) until post-launch smoothing completes.
action_items: (A) Validation: run synthetic spike tests targeting us-east4 and europe-west1 during next maintenance window (JIRA-OPS-1243)
(B) Autoscaler tuning: reduce cool-down from 2m to 90s for low-latency tiers and increase max-batch size limit to reduce per-token cost
(C) Warm pool playbook: instrument warm-pool health checks and automatic promotion policy; owner: Mateo
(D) Cost/commitment: finance to model 6-month reserved commit for 120 GPUs in us-west1 to lower unit cost; owner: Priya
(E) Observability: add a 'runway-hours' panel to Console per-route/dashboard (contrib: Chen)
sizing_rationale: Absorptive buffer = max(0, 95th-committed) rounded up to nearest 10 GPUs. Warm failover reserve tuned to cover regional failure for top-3 customers while keeping latency within SLA drain time. Global buffer uses conservative correlation factor (0.6) to account for partially correlated spikes across regions.
risk_notes: If cross-region egress or throughput throttles during failover, effective absorptive capacity drops ~20-30%. Spot reclaim rates in APAC can spike during cloud maintenance windows; plan for temporary re-routing to us-west1 with throttling rules. If Dedicated commit growth outpaces fleet expansion, shortfall may exceed buffer — tie commit growth to infra capacity run rate.
analysis_notes:
- Early drafts show larger buffers (350+) but cost tradeoffs unacceptable; this is compromise.
